s: The story of Moses is one of the most beautiful and exciting stories in the whole world.
It grabs hold of us and never stops being interesting, not even for a moment. It is told so vividly that once you hear it, you never forget it.
I have often imagined how worried everyone was when that child was born. He came into the world with a death sentence hanging over him. Pharaoh had ordered that all the baby boys must die.
But his mother refused to obey even the king's command. She made up her mind that her child would live. So right from the start, the battle of right against power was fought at a baby's cradle.
Moses' mother was a slave woman.
She had to work in the brickyards or in the fields. But God was on her side, and she won. A mother always wins when God is on her side.

Before she went to work, she had to find a place to hide her child. She put his little sister, Miriam, on guard. Meanwhile she kept out of sight of Pharaoh's soldiers, who were searching everywhere to kill the Jewish baby boys.
She kept him hidden for three months. She may have found a new hiding place every few days.
It is hard to think of anything harder than hiding a healthy, growing baby. Yet he stayed hidden for three whole months.
By now he had grown bigger and livelier, so a safer hiding place had to be found. I can picture this mother giving up her rest and sleep to build a little floating ark to save her child.
I believe the plan must have come from heaven.

I have often thought that God must have cared about that work as much as Moses' mother did. You can't make me believe that something so important, with such huge results, just happened by luck or chance.
Maybe God whispered the plan to her when she came to Him in prayer. She was grieving, because she was afraid Pharaoh's sword would kill her child.
And how carefully she had to choose the material to make the ark!
I think she checked every twig carefully so that nothing weak would end up in it. As she wove that ark, she wove into it her heart, her soul, her prayers and her tears.

Oh, mothers, if only you took that much care over the friends your children spend time with, the books they read and the places they go! Then there would not be so many girls ending up in the red-light district. And there would not be so many boys growing up to live as criminals.

And how thankfully she must have poured out her heart when the work was finally done! The ark was ready to carry its precious cargo. That cargo was more precious than if it had held the crown jewels of Egypt.
I can picture the last night that baby spent at home.

Some of you can probably remember the last night your baby was alive. You remember the last night the coffin stayed in your home. And you remember how the pallbearers and the hearse came the next day.
Others in the house may have slept soundly, but you could not sleep. And I imagine Moses' mother could not sleep either.

blocks.x:
"There are toy whips and tops and pieces of string
And shoes that no little feet will wear;
There are bits of ribbon and broken wings
And curls of golden hair.

"There are pretty little jackets that no one wears,
There are toys and model ships;
There are books and pictures, faded and torn
And marked by the fingertips
Of little dimpled hands that have turned to dust—
Still we try to believe that the Lord is fair.

"Still, a bitter feeling fills our soul,
Even when we try to pray,
Because Death spared so many other flowers
And took ours away.
And sometimes we doubt that the Lord can know
How much our broken hearts loved them so.

"But then we think of our loved ones who have died,
Our children who will never grow old,
And how they are waiting and watching for us
In the city with streets of gold;
And how they are safe through all the years
From sickness and hunger and war.
With tears running down, we thank our great God
For the things in the cabinet drawer."
A Mother Keeps Watch

s: Others in the house might have slept. But she could not waste a single moment of the precious time she had left with her little one. All through the night she must have prayed. She asked God to shield and protect her baby, to bless the work she had done, and to bless the step she was about to take.
People often ask me, "I wonder what the angels do. How do they spend their time?"
I think I know what some of them were doing that night.
You can be sure they were not off at some card party.
They guarded that house so closely that not one of old Pharaoh's soldiers ever stepped through the door.
They made sure that none of those soldiers hurt that baby.

At dawn the mother must have kissed him goodbye. She put him in the ark and hid him among the tall reeds. Then, with an aching heart and eyes full of tears, she went back to the field and the brickyards. There she worked and waited to see what God would do.
She had prayed and done her very best. When you have done that, you can count on God to give you the help you need.
If only we believed that with God everything is possible, no matter how unlikely it seems! Then the Lord would answer our prayers in ways we never expected.
She knew God would help her somehow. But I don't think she ever dreamed that God would do it by sending Pharaoh's own daughter to take care of the child.
It was no harder for God to send the princess than to get the mother to build the ark.
What seemed impossible to her was easy for God.
Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river to bathe. The ark was found, just as God wanted. One of her servant girls was sent to bring it to her.
You often wonder what the angels are up to.
I think some of the angels rounded up the crocodiles on the far side of the Nile. That kept them from finding Moses and eating him.
You can be sure all of heaven was watching to make sure not one hair on that baby's head was hurt.
All the devils in hell put together could not have pulled a single hair out of its head.

The ark was brought to her. With a woman's curiosity, Pharaoh's daughter just had to look inside to see what was there. When they took off the cover, there lay a strong, healthy baby boy. He was kicking his heels and sucking his thumbs, as most of us probably did when we were boys, and as you probably did when you were a girl.
The baby looks up and cries. Those tears wiped out everything that was against it and gave it a chance to live.
I don't know for sure, but I think an angel stood there and pinched it to make it cry. It certainly cried at just the right time.
That's just how God plans things.
God always acts at just the right time.
Give God a chance. He may seem a little slow sometimes, but He will always show up in time.
That baby's tears were the jewels that paid for Israel's freedom from slavery in Egypt.
The princess had a woman's heart. And when a woman's heart meets a baby's tears, something happens that makes the devil lose his nerve.
Maybe the princess had lost a baby of her own. Seeing Moses may have torn that old wound open and made it bleed again.
But she had a woman's heart. It made her forget that she was Pharaoh's daughter, and she made up her mind to protect that baby.
Faithful Miriam (praise the Lord for Miriam!) could see the princess's feelings showing on her face.

Miriam had studied people's faces so much that she could read the princess's heart like an open book. So she said to her, "Shall I go and find one of the Hebrew women to nurse the baby for you?" And the princess said, "Go."

I can see her little feet and legs flying as she runs down the hot, dusty road. Her mother must have seen her coming a mile away. And she ran to meet her and have her own baby placed back in her arms.
And she was even paid in Egyptian gold to take care of her own baby!
Do you see how the Lord works?
"Now take this child and take care of it for me, and I will pay you your wages."
The joke was on Pharaoh's daughter. She was paying Moses' mother to do what she wanted to do more than anything else—take care of her own baby.

How quickly the mother was repaid for those long hours of worry, fear and grief! If the angels know what is happening down here, heaven must have been full of joy and laughter when they saw Moses and Miriam back at home, safe under the protection of Pharaoh's daughter.
I imagine she fell to her knees and poured out her heart to God, who had helped her in such a wonderful way.
She must have said, "Well, Lord, I knew You would help me.

I knew You would take care of my baby when I made the ark, put him in it and set it in the water. But I never dreamed You would put him back in my arms for me to look after. Now I don't have to slave away in the field making bricks. And I don't have to be tortured almost to death with fear that Pharaoh's soldiers will find my baby and kill him.
I never thought You would soften Pharaoh's hard heart and make him pay me to do what I would rather do than anything else in the world."
I expect to meet Moses' mother in heaven, and I'm going to ask her how much old Pharaoh had to pay her for that job.
I think that's one of the best jokes ever. That old sinner had to pay the mother to take care of her own baby!
But I tell you, if you give God a chance, He will fill your heart until it overflows.
All you have to do is give Him a chance.

blocks.x: A Mother's Courage

s: This mother had amazing courage.
Everything was against her, but she refused to give up.
She never lost heart.
She fought as bravely as any man ever fought with cannons booming and rifles roaring around him.

blocks.x:
"The bravest battle that was ever fought—
Shall I tell you where and when?
You won't find it on the maps of the world—
It was fought by the mothers of men.

"No, it wasn't fought with cannons or bullets,
With swords or with a noble pen,
No, not with the powerful words or ideas
That come from the mouths of great men.

"But deep inside a woman's hidden heart—
The hearts of women who would not give in,
But bravely and silently did their part—
Look, that is the battlefield.

"No troops lining up, no songs around the campfire,
No flag to shine and wave;
But oh, these battles last so long—
From babyhood to the grave."

s: Mothers are always brave when their children's safety is at stake.
This happened out West.
A mother was working in her garden, and her little child was sitting under a tree in the yard, playing.

The mother heard the child scream and ran to it. A huge snake was wrapping itself around the baby. As the snake's head swung around, she jumped and grabbed it by the neck. She tore it off her baby and threw it hard against a tree.
Fathers often quit.

The man of the house often starts drinking, wastes his life away, takes poison and kills himself. But the mother will stand by the home and keep the little family together. She will do it even if the only manicure her fingernails ever get is scrubbing clothes on a washboard.
If men had half as much grit as women, the stories of many homes would be very different.
Just look at the work she does!
It is the greatest work in the world. Its importance reaches so far that it rises high above everything else in the universe. Her job is to mold hearts and lives and to shape character.
If you want to find greatness, don't go to a king's throne. Go to a baby's cradle. The closer you get to the cradle, the closer you get to greatness.
Now, when Jesus wanted to teach His disciples a lesson they would never forget, did He call in a college professor?
Not a chance. He brought in a little child and said, "Unless you become like one of these, you will never enter the kingdom of God."
This work is so important that God will trust nobody but a mother with it.
Sending a boy or girl out into life to live for Christ is a greater job than launching a battleship.
Moses was a special instrument chosen by the Lord. God wanted him to get the right start in life, so He gave him a good mother.
There wasn't a college professor in all of Egypt that God would trust with that baby! So He put the child back in its mother's arms.
He knew that the best person on earth to trust with that baby was its own mother.
When God sends us great men, He wants them to have the right start.
So He makes sure they have a good mother.
Just about any old stick will do for a dad.
But God is very choosy about mothers.

blocks.x: We Need Good Mothers

s: So the great need of this country, or any other country, is good mothers. And I believe America has more good mothers than any other nation on earth.
If Washington's mother had been like a Happy Hooligan's mother, Washington would have grown up to be a Happy Hooligan.
Someone once said, "God couldn't be everywhere, so He gave us mothers."

That may sound like poetry, but it is true that "the hand that rocks the cradle rules the world." If every cradle were rocked by a good mother, the world would be full of good men, as sure as you are breathing.
If every boy and girl today had a good mother, the bars and the brothels would be out of business by tomorrow.
One time a young man joined a church, and the preacher asked him, "What did I say that made you decide to become a Christian?"
The young man answered, "It wasn't anything I heard you say. It was the way my mother lived."
I tell you, one ounce of example weighs more than forty million tons of theory and guesswork.
If mothers lived the way they should, we preachers would have very little to do.
Keep the devil out of the boys and girls, and he will have to leave the world.
The old sinners will die off if we keep the young ones pure.
The biggest place in the world belongs to the people who work closely with young people.

Being a king, an emperor or a president is a very small thing compared to being a mother or a teacher of children, whether in a public school or a Sunday school. Their places are so great that every angel in heaven would gladly throw in a whole basket of diamonds for the chance to come down here and take their place.
Compared with training a boy or girl, commanding an army is not much more than sweeping a street or hammering on an anvil.
Moses' mother did more for the world than all the kings Egypt ever had.
Teaching a child to love the truth and hate lies, to love purity and hate sin, is a greater thing than inventing a flying machine that could take you to the moon before breakfast.
Without even knowing it, you start influences moving that will either curse or bless this old universe. They can bring new worlds out of chaos and change them for God.

blocks.x: God's Own Hall of Fame

s: A man once sent a friend of mine some crystals and said, "Just one of these crystals, no bigger than the point of a pin, will turn sixteen huge barrels of water a clear green color."
Think of it! There is enough power in one tiny speck to color sixteen huge barrels of water.
A single word or action has the power to ruin a boy, and through him to bring a curse on a whole community.
There is also enough power in a word to color that child's whole life, so that the child becomes a power that lifts the world to Jesus Christ.
Mothers start influences moving that will reach either heaven or hell.
Talk about greatness!
Oh, just wait until you reach the mountains of eternity! Then read the mothers' names in God's hall of fame, and you will see what they have been in this world.
Wait until you see God's hall of fame. In it you will see women bent over the washtub.

I want to tell you women something. Wasting your time hugging and kissing a poodle, petting a "Spitz" dog, drinking fancy brandy drinks and cocktails at parties, and playing cards is a very small thing compared to shaping the life of a child.
So tell me, where did Moses get his faith?
From his mother. Where did Moses get the courage to say, "I refuse to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter"?
It came from his mother.
Where did Moses get the nerve to say "Excuse me, please" to the pleasures of Egypt?
He got that from his mother too.
You can be sure he didn't pick it up from his dad.
Plenty of boys would have turned out better if their old dad had died before they were born.
You tell your son to stay away from bad company.
But sometimes when he walks down the street with his father, he is with the worst company in town.
His dad smokes, drinks and chews tobacco.
Moses got all this from his mother.
He was educated in all the wisdom of Egypt, but it didn't make him big-headed.
When God wants to fling a world out into space, He doesn't worry about it.
The first mile that world travels sets its path forever.
But when God sends a child out into the world, He cares very much that it gets a good start.
The Catholics are right when they say, "Let us have the children until they are ten, and after that we don't care who has them."
The Catholics aren't losing any sleep worrying about men and women leaving their church.
It is the only church that has ever shown us the one sensible way to reach the masses of people. That way is to get hold of the children.
That's the only way on God's earth you will ever solve the problem of reaching the masses.
Get the boys and girls started right, and the devil will hang a black mourning ribbon on his door and let his fires die down. Hell will be up for rent before the Fourth of July!
A friend of mine had to take her little girl to the hospital for an operation.
They thought she would be scared, but she said, "I don't mind, as long as Mama is there to hold my hand."

They got her ready for the operation and led her into the room. They put her on the table, placed the cone over her face and soaked it with ether. Then she said, "Now, Mama, take my hand and hold it, and I won't be afraid."
So the mother stood there and held her hand.
The operation was done. When she woke up, they asked her, "Bessie, weren't you afraid when they put you on the table?"
She said, "No, Mama stood right there and held my hand.
I wasn't scared."
A mother's hand has great power.
There is more power in a woman's hand than in a king's royal staff.
There is great power in a mother's kiss, too. A mother's kiss gives inspiration, courage, hope and ambition.
One kiss made Benjamin West a painter, and he remembered it all his life.
One kiss can chase away a child's fear in the dark and make the little one brave.
It gives strength where there is weakness.

One day I was in a town and saw a mother out with her boy. He had big steel braces on both legs, all the way up to his hips. When I got close enough, I could tell from their talk that this was not the first time his mother had taken him out for a walk.
She was taking him out to exercise so he could learn to use his legs.
He was struggling, but she smiled and said, "You're doing great today—better than yesterday."
Then she bent down and kissed him. That encouraging kiss made him try even harder. She said, "You're doing wonderfully, son."
And he said, "Mama, I'm going to run. Watch me!"
He started off, but one of his toes caught on the steel brace of his other leg, and he stumbled. She caught him, kissed him and said, "That was fine, son. You did so well!"
He tried it because his mother had encouraged him with a kiss.
He wasn't trying to show off.
Nothing helps and inspires a person's life like a mother's kiss.

blocks.x:
"If we knew those little baby fingers pressed against the window
Would be cold and still tomorrow, never to bother us again,
Would our darling's bright eyes ever see a frown on our face?

"Let's gather up the sunbeams lying all along our path,
Let's keep the wheat and roses and throw out the thorns and husks!
We will find our sweetest comfort in the blessings of today,
As with patient hands we clear the prickly weeds from our way."
A Mother's Singing

s: A mother's song has power too.
It's the best music the world has ever heard.
The best music in the world is like the best biscuits—it's the kind Mother makes.
No brass band or pipe organ comes anywhere close to Mother's singing.
Calvé, Melba, Nordica, Eames, Schumann-Heink—they're nothing special compared to Mother.
They can't really sing at all.
They don't even know the basics of the kind of music Mother sings.
Her kind of music wraps itself around your heart.
Heaven's music would disappoint me if there were no mothers there to sing.
The song of an angel or any other heavenly being would not mean much to me.
What would an angel's song mean to you if there were no mother's song?
A mother's song is sweeter than any song ever sung by a singer or written by a poet.
Talk about beautiful poems! You should hear a mother sing when her baby is at her breast and her heart is full of feeling.
Her voice may not impress an expert, but it will please anyone who has a heart.
The songs that have moved the world are not the ones written by the great composers.
In my opinion, the best music is not the perfect performance of these expensive opera singers.
No art in the world can turn into a melody the happiness that our connections and memories bring.
I think when we get to heaven we will find that some of the best songs we sing there are the ones we learned at our mother's knee.

blocks.x: A Mother's Love

s: A mother's love has power.
A mother's love must be a lot like God's love.
I have often wondered how God could ever have told the world He loved it without a mother's help.
If the devils in hell ever turned pale with fear, it was on the day a mother's love first blazed up in a woman's heart.
In my opinion, if the devil ever got scared, it was on that day.
You know that a mother has to love her baby even before it is born.
Like God, she has to go into the dark valley of death to bring it into the world. She will love her child and suffer for it. The child can grow up and become wicked, and still she will love it.
Nothing will make her blame her child. And I think, women, that one of the most awful things about hell will be that there is no mother's love there.
In hell there is nothing but black, bottomless, endless, eternal hate—no mother's love.

blocks.x:
"And even if he crawls through the worst caves of sin,
And crouches, maybe, with bleary, bloodshot eyes,
Under the hangman's rope—his mother's lips
Will kiss him in his last bed of shame,
And love him even for what she hoped he would be."

s: I thank God for what a mother's love has done for the world.
Oh, there is power in what God trusts a mother with.
Just as surely as the princess put Moses into his mother's arms, God has put your babies into your arms. He has given them to you to raise and care for.
Every child is placed in a mother's arms as something God trusts her with. She will have to answer to God for the way she treats that child.
No mother on God's earth has any right to raise her children just for pleasure.
She has no right to send them to dancing school and to places full of sin.
You have no right to do things that will bring a curse on your children.
That baby is placed in your arms so you can train it for the Lord.
A mother has no more right to raise her children for pleasure than I have to pick your pocket or throw red pepper in your eyes.
She has no more right to do that than a bank teller has to rob the vault and steal people's savings.
One of the worst sins you can commit is to be unfaithful with what has been trusted to you.

blocks.x: A Mother's Duty

s: "Take this child and take care of it for me."
That is your whole job with it.
That child is a jewel that belongs to God. He gives it to you to polish for Him so He can set it in a crown.
Who knows? Maybe Judas became the godless, worthless wretch he was because he had a godless, worthless mother.
Do you know? I sure don't.
What is more to blame for our crowded prisons than mothers?

And who is more to blame for the crowded brothels than you, who let your children run the streets with every Tom, Dick and Harry? You let them hang around with some little good-for-nothing whose character is so dark it would leave a black mark on a piece of tar paper!
I have talked with men in prisons who cursed their mothers right in front of me.
Why? Because they blame their mothers for the place they ended up in.
"Take the child and take care of it for me, and I will pay you your wages."
God pays in joy that fire can't burn, hunger can't touch and the devil can't steal.
He will pay you, so don't worry.
So make sure your name is on God's payroll.
"Take this child and take care of it for me, and I will pay you your wages."
If you haven't been doing that, then get your name on God's payroll now.
"Take this child and take care of it for me, and I will pay you your wages."
Then think of your responsibility! It is so great that I don't see how any woman could fail to be a Christian and serve God.
What do you think God will do if a mother fails?
The thought of it almost knocks me over.
What if, because you were unfaithful, your son becomes a curse and your daughter a disgrace?
What if, because you neglected him, that boy becomes a Judas when he could have been a John or a Paul?
Some years ago in Cincinnati, a mother went to the zoo. She stood leaning over the bear pit, watching the bears and tossing them crumbs and peanuts.
She was holding her baby in her arms. The baby was a year and three months old.
She was so busy watching the bears that the baby wriggled out of her arms and fell into the pit. She had to watch those huge beasts tear it to pieces.
For the rest of her life it will be a real hell for her to know that her little one died because of her own carelessness and neglect!
"Take this child and bring it up for me, and I will pay you your wages."

Will you make a promise, a solemn agreement, with God, with me and with one another? Will you promise that from now on, with God's help, you will try harder than ever before to raise your children for God?

"I once read a story about an angel who slipped out of heaven and came to this world one bright, sunny day. He wandered through fields, forests, cities and villages. As the sun went down, he got his wings ready for the flight home.
The angel said, "My visit is over. Before I go back, I must collect some souvenirs of my trip."

He looked at the beautiful flowers in the garden and said, "How lovely they are, and how sweet they smell!" He picked the rarest roses and made a bouquet. Then he said, "I can't see anything more beautiful and sweet-smelling than these flowers."

The angel looked further and saw a bright-eyed, rosy-cheeked child. He said, "That baby is prettier than the flowers. I'll take that too." Then, looking back at the cradle, he saw a mother's love pouring out over her baby like a gushing spring. The angel said, "That mother's love is the most beautiful thing I have seen!
I'll take that too."
With these three treasures the angel flew to the pearly gates of heaven. He said, "Before I go, I must look over the souvenirs of my trip to earth."
He looked at the flowers. They had wilted.
He looked at the baby's smile, and it had faded away.
He looked at the mother's love, and it was still shining with all its first beauty.

So he threw away the dead flowers and tossed aside the faded smile. Holding the mother's love close to his heart, he swept through the gates into the city. He shouted that the only thing he had found that kept its sweetness all the way from earth to heaven was a mother's love.
"Take this child and take care of it for me, and I will pay you your wages."
Someone once asked Napoleon Bonaparte, "What do you think France needs most?" He answered, "Mothers, mothers, mothers."
You women can turn a home into a hell or into a heaven.
Don't let your tongue loose like a machine gun, tearing into everybody. Don't tear into your husbands and drive them out of their homes.
If I wanted to find out how godly you really are, I would ask the girl who works for you.

All this talk about "the land of the free" doesn't count for much when the children look like a rummage sale in a secondhand shop. Their hair isn't combed, their pants are ripped, their buttons are missing and their stockings are hanging down.
You don't need great wisdom to see that Mother is too busy with her social events, her clubs and so on to pay much attention to the kids.

blocks.x: The Mothers of Famous Men

s: Nero's mother was a murderer, so it's no wonder he played the fiddle while Rome burned.
Patrick Henry's mother was a gifted speaker. That is why every schoolboy and schoolgirl knows his words, "Give me liberty or give me death."
Coleridge's mother taught him Bible stories from the pictures on the old Dutch tiles around the fireplace.
Today homes need authority more than at any other time in the history of this nation.

In the thick of the fight I have come up against every kind of man and beast you can imagine. And I am convinced that neither the law nor the gospel can build a nation without authority and good example in the home.
We need those two things.
A boy who has a healthy home and surroundings, with wise discipline too, doesn't often end up in reform school.
Susanna Wesley was the mother of nineteen children, and she kept them all for God.
When someone asked her how she did it, she answered, "I got hold of their hearts while they were young, and I never let go."

George Washington's mother argued hard against it. If she hadn't, George Washington would have become a young officer-in-training in the British navy, and the capital city over there would have some other name.
John Randolph said in the House of Representatives, "If it hadn't been for my godly mother, I, John Randolph, would have been an unbeliever."
Gray, who wrote the poem "Elegy in a Country Churchyard," said he was one of a large family of children who had the bad luck of outliving their mother.
And I believe the ideal mother is the fruit of a civilization that grew out of the manger in Bethlehem.
I am sure every angel in heaven would be glad to come to earth and have the honor of being a mother, if God would allow it.

What a wonderful thing it must be, at the end of your life on earth, to look back on a noble and godly life! You will know you did all you could to help leave this old world to God. You gave your tears and your prayers, and you taught your children to fear God. So when you are gone, your noble character will live on in your children.

I believe in blood. I believe in good blood and bad blood, honest blood and thieving blood, brave blood and cowardly blood. I believe in pure blood and immoral blood, in drinking blood and sober blood.

The lips of the Hapsburgs show immorality. The lips of the Stuarts show cruelty, prejudice and lust, from Mary, Queen of Scots, down to Charles I and Charles II, and James I—who showed the world what a foolish Scotsman can be like when he is a fool—all the way down to King James II.
Scottish blood means stubbornness.
They never quit.
I should know—Mrs. Sunday is completely Scottish.
English blood shows deep respect for the English.
You can see that from the fact that England recently spent $50,000,000 to put a crown on George's head.
Danish blood shows a love for the sea.
Welsh blood shows religious passion and eagerness for God.
Jewish blood shows a love of money, from Abraham's day until now.
You may have read this story. In New York there was a woman who said to her son, who was a drunk, "Let's go down to the police court and have the judge send you over to the island for a few weeks.
Maybe then you'll straighten out, and I can respect you again."
So they went down to the police court and stood before the judge.
He asked who was bringing the charge. The mother jumped forward, ready to speak.
Then she stopped short. She turned to her son, threw her arms around his neck and cried out, "I can't!
I can't! He is my son. I love him, and I can't."
Then she fell down dead at his feet.
She loved her drunken, bloated, lazy son so dearly that she could not stand up and judge him.
"So I tell you, people will be forgiven for every kind of sin and blasphemy. But blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
"Anyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, not in this world and not in the world to come."
I would like to know where anyone ever found any grounds for believing that people get a second chance after death.
Jesus Christ was either human or He was divine.
If He was only human, then I don't have to obey His words any more than the words of any other philosopher.
The Pharisees accused Jesus of working together with the devil.
They said to Him, "You have a devil in You."
They grew bolder in attacking Him. They said, "You do what You do through Beelzebub, the prince of devils."
Jesus said, "How can that be?
If I do My works through the devil, then explain why I am tearing down the devil's works.
If I am a devil, and if I work through the devil, then I would not be working to damage the devil's works.
I would not be doing what I do to destroy the devil's works. Instead, I would be working to destroy God's works."
From that day on, they did not dare to ask Him any more questions.
I know people have many different opinions about what the sin against the Holy Spirit really is.
Some think it could only be committed by people who heard Jesus Christ speak and saw Him in person.
If that is true, then you and I are not in danger. Neither of us has ever seen Jesus in person or heard Him.

Others think people have committed it since Jesus' time, but only very rarely. And a third group think they have committed it themselves. They spend their lives in gloom and fear. They are completely useless to themselves and to everyone around them.

And yet I have no doubt at all that thousands of people fit what I am talking about. They are never gloomy, never depressed, never discouraged. Their conscience is at peace. Their spirits are light and happy. They eat three meals a day and sleep like a baby at night. Nothing seems to bother them. Life is all fun and song.

blocks.x: What It Is

s: Please set aside any ideas you have had, or still have, about what the sin against the Holy Spirit is—the unpardonable sin. And please listen to me. I have read every sermon on this subject that I could get my hands on. I have listened to every preacher I ever had the chance to hear. And I have read everything the Bible teaches about it.

I don't claim that my views on this are perfect. But I have wept and prayed and studied over it. If there is time, and if my strength and your patience last, I will try to ask and answer a few questions.
What is it? Why won't God forgive it?
It is not swearing.
If swearing were the unpardonable sin, many men in heaven would have to go to hell. And crowds of people on earth who are on their way to heaven would have to go to hell too.
It is not drunkenness.
Crowds of people in heaven have crept and crawled out of the swamps of filth and the sewers of sin and drunkenness.
Some of the brightest lights that ever shone for God were men God saved from drunkenness.
It is not adultery. Jesus spoke to a woman who was caught in the very act of adultery. He said, "I don't condemn you either. Go and sin no more."
It is not stealing. Jesus said to Zaccheus, "Today salvation has come to your house."
Zaccheus had been a thief.
It is not murder. Men have had blood on their hands, and God has forgiven them.
The apostle Paul had blood on his hands.
What is it? To me it is plain and simple.
It is rejecting Jesus Christ as your Savior—again and again, without stopping, and then for the last time.
God offers you mercy and salvation. And you say, "No," and push it aside.
I do know that every man and woman gets a last call.
God says His Spirit will not always strive with people. When God's Spirit strives with someone for the last time and that person says "No," their doom is sealed forever.
It is not one special kind of sin. It is not one single act.
It might be swearing. It might be stealing.

Any sin becomes unpardonable if God keeps calling you to give it up and you keep refusing. If you don't give it up, He will pull back and leave you alone. Then that sin will become unpardonable, because God will not ask you again to give it up.
It is not one shocking act. It is doing the same thing over and over again.
A time will come when you commit that sin one time too many.
It is a known law of the mind: when you resist the truth, it loses its power over you.
You hear a truth for the first time, and you reject it.
The next time, that truth won't seem as strong. It will be easier to resist.
God throws a truth in your face.
You reject it. He throws it again. You reject it again.
At last God will stop throwing the truth at you. Then you will have committed the unpardonable sin.

blocks.x:
"There is a line we cannot see.
It crosses every path.
It is God's border between
His patience and His anger.

"To cross that line is to die,
to die without knowing it.
Your eyes may still be bright,
your health may still glow.

"Your conscience may still be at peace,
your spirits light and happy.
What pleased you may still please you,
and you may toss your cares away.

"But God has put a mark on that forehead,
a mark that cannot be removed.
People cannot see it, for people
are still blind and in the dark.

"In fact, the doomed one's path here on earth
may bloom like the Garden of Eden.
He does not know it and will not know it.
He will not believe that he is doomed."

s: In Scotland there are men who make their living by gathering birds' eggs. The birds lay them on rock ledges far below the top of the cliff.
The men tie a rope to a tree and to themselves. Then they swing back and forth, and in onto the rock ledge.
Years ago a man was doing this very thing. The rope under his arms came untied. Because the rock stuck out, the rope hung many feet out of his reach.
The man waited for help, but no help came.
Night came, and then morning. He gave up and expected to starve to death. He felt there was no way out. Then a breeze picked up, and the hanging rope began to move.

As the wind grew stronger, the rope swung more and more. As it swung in, he said, "If I miss it, I die. If I grab it, it's my only chance." He prayed to God. As the rope swung in, he leaped out over the drop and grabbed it. He pulled himself up, hand over hand, to the top. When he got there, his hair was as white as snow.
There is one rope that swings through this old world today—the Holy Spirit.
With every invitation, it swings farther away.
We are living in the last age, the age of the Holy Spirit. And God is speaking to the world through the Holy Spirit today.

blocks.x: Resisting the Truth

s: By every known law of the mind, people are converted when the truth works on their minds.
Every time you resist the truth, it has less power over your mind the next time you hear it.
And every time you hear a truth and fight against it, you get stronger at resisting the truth.
We all know this: each time you resist, you grow stronger against the truth.
When someone hears the truth and resists it, the truth grows weaker. And that person grows stronger in resisting it.
No matter what Jesus Christ did, the Jews refused to believe.

He had done amazing things, but they would not believe. So when Lazarus was dead, Jesus said, "Lazarus, come out!" Then He turned to the Jews and said, "Isn't that enough proof that I am the Son of God?" And they shouted, "Away with Him!"
One day He was walking along a hot, dusty road. He met a funeral procession.
The mourners were carrying the body of a young man. His mother was weeping.
Jesus told them to put the coffin down on the ground. Then He said:
"Young man, get up!" And he got up.
Then He asked the Pharisees, "I make the dead rise. Isn't that enough proof that I am the Son of God?" And they shouted, "Away with Him!"
So no matter what Jesus did, the Jews refused to believe Him.
And no matter what Jesus Christ says or does today, you will refuse to accept Him. You will keep rushing headlong toward eternal damnation.

blocks.x: "Too Late"

s: Jesus Christ gives you just as much proof today.
My friend Mrs. Robinson was preaching down in Indiana.
I don't remember the town, but I think it was Kokomo. I do remember what happened. On the last day she tried to get the leader of high society there to give her heart to God.
She preached. Then she went down into the aisle and talked with her.
Then she went back to the platform and made her appeal from there.
She went to the girl again, but the girl still refused.
As Mrs. Robinson turned to leave, she saw the girl borrow a pencil from the man with her. The girl wrote something in the back of a hymnbook.
A few years later Mrs. Robinson went back to that town. She was told the girl was dying.
They told her the doctors had just met together. They had said she would not live until night.
Mrs. Robinson hurried to her home.
The girl looked up and recognized her. She said, "I didn't send for you.
You came on your own, and you're too late."
Every time Mrs. Robinson pleaded with her, she answered, "You're too late."
At last she said, "Go and look in the hymnbook at the church."
They hurried to the church and looked through the hymnbooks. In the back of one they found her name and address and these words: "I'll run the risk. I'll take my chance."
That was her last call.
No one sin is the unpardonable sin. But it may be doing it over and over and over again, until God says, "Take it and go to hell."
Who can commit it?
I used to think only wicked and foul-mouthed people could commit it.
Whom did Jesus warn?
The Pharisees. And who were they?
The most moral men in Jerusalem.
Who can commit it?
Any man or woman who says "No" to Jesus Christ.
You may even defend the Bible.
You may be the most moral man or woman in the world.

Your name may stand for goodness and purity. But let God try to get into your heart. Let Him try to get you to walk down the aisle and openly confess Jesus Christ. Then your heart and lips are locked tight like a bank vault. And God has not been able to pull you to your feet.
And God will not keep begging you to do it.
Something may say to you, "I ought to be a Christian."
This is the age of the Holy Spirit.
God has spoken in three ages.
First, through the old law of Moses.
Then Jesus Christ came to this earth and lived here. And the Jews and the Gentiles plotted together to kill Him.
Then the Holy Spirit came down at Pentecost. And God is speaking through the Holy Spirit today.
The Holy Spirit is urging you to become a Christian.

It takes the whole Trinity working together to keep you out of hell. It takes God the Father to provide the plan of salvation, the Holy Spirit to convict you, and Jesus Christ to redeem you through His blood. And it takes your acceptance and repentance to save you.
Sin is no small thing.

blocks.x: The Trinity's Representative

s: The Holy Spirit is the only representative of the Trinity in the world today.
Jesus has been here, but He is not here now—not in flesh and blood.
The Holy Spirit is here now.
When He leaves the world, it's good-bye.
There was an old saint of God who is now in glory.
Once he was holding meetings. A young man came down the aisle and even asked him to pray for him.
The old man said, "Let's settle it now." But the young man refused. He just told him to pray for him.
Years later, the old saint was in a hotel in Philadelphia. He was waiting for his card to be taken up to the man he wanted to see.
He looked in through the door of the bar.
A young man was there ordering a drink.
The two saw each other's reflections in the big mirror behind the bar. The young man came out and said, "How do you do?"
The old man greeted him.
The young man said, "I suppose you don't remember me?" The old saint had to admit that he didn't.
The young man asked if he remembered a meeting in New York eleven years before. At that meeting a young man had come down the aisle and asked him to pray for him.
He said he was that young man.
The old saint said, "From what I have just seen, I guess you did not settle it."
The young man said, "I didn't, and I never plan to.
I believe there is a hell, and I'm going there as fast as I can."
The old man begged him to be quiet. But he said, "It's true.
If Jesus Christ came through that door right now, I would spit in His face."
The old man said, "Don't talk that way.
I would not let you talk about my wife like that. And I will not let you talk about Christ like that."
The young man said it was all true.
The old man said, "Maybe it is all true, but I don't like to hear it."
The young man said it was true. He said that if he had a Bible, he would tear it up.
Swearing one oath after another, he went to the bar. He had two or three drinks and walked out the door.
Sometimes it may be total, complete indifference.
Some people can hear any sermon and any song and not be moved.
I'd guess that some of you have not been convicted of sin for twenty-five years.
Back then God's Spirit convicted you, and you did not give in.
The first place I ever preached was the little town of Garner, in Hancock County, Iowa. A man came down the aisle there.
I said, "Who's that?" Someone told me he was one of the richest men in the county.
I asked him what I had said that helped him. He said, "Nothing."
Then he told me that twenty-one years before, he had gone to Chicago. He had sold his livestock four hours before he had to catch a train.
Moody was in town. So he and a friend went and stood inside the door, listening to the sermon.
When Moody gave the invitation, the man handed his coat and hat to his friend. He said he was going down to shake Moody's hand.
His friend told him not to do it. He said he would miss his train, and after that day his railroad pass would be no good.
The man said he could afford to pay his own way home.
His friend told him not to go up there with all the excitement. He told him to wait and settle it at home.
The man said he had waited thirty-five years and had not settled it at home. But his friend kept urging him not to go forward and give his heart to God.
At last the time was gone. They had to catch the train, and the man had not gone forward.
He told me he had never had a desire to give his heart to God until that time, twenty-one years later, when he heard me preach.
The Spirit called him when he heard Moody. Then the Spirit did not call him again until twenty-one years later, when he heard me.
I have never said, and I never will say, that all unbelievers died in agony.
Usually people die the way they have lived.
If you have lived in unbelief, in ninety-nine cases out of a hundred you will die that way.
If Christianity is a good thing to die with, it is a good thing to live with.

blocks.x: Deathbed Confessions

s: I don't put much trust in these deathbed confessions.
A deathbed confession is like burning a candle at both ends and then blowing the smoke in Jesus' face.
A deathbed confession is like drinking the cup of life and then offering the dregs to Christ.

Some people keep control of their own lives until the very last moment. Then they try to sneak into the kingdom because Jesus Christ is patient and merciful. I think that is one of the most shameful, miserable, low-down things you can do. It is unworthy of any man or woman.
I don't say that none of them are real.
But there is only one in the Bible. That was the first time the dying thief had ever heard of Christ, and he accepted Him right away.
So your case is not like his.
You have had wagonloads of sermons dumped on you. But it is very hard to accept Christ at the last moment.

Maybe you have lived without conviction. Then at your funeral the preacher may not put you in the front row of heaven, with a harp in your hands and a crown on your head. If he doesn't, your friends should not get angry.
God can forgive sins, but you have to meet His conditions.
He does not want anyone to perish. But He has the right to tell you and me what to do to be saved.
A doctor had practiced medicine for sixty years. He was asked how many godless men he had seen show any sign of concern on their deathbeds.
He said he had kept track of three hundred, and only three had shown any real concern.
That shocks me.
Usually you die the way you have lived.
A minister was called to a brothel to be with a dying girl in her last moments.
He prayed. Then he looked at her face, but he saw no sign of hope that she would repent.

He felt led to pray again. This time he felt led to include a Bible verse, Isaiah 1:18: "Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord. Even if your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow. Even if they are red like crimson, they will be like wool."
"Is that what the Bible says?" the girl asked.
He said it was.
"Would you let me see it?" And the minister showed it to her.
"Would you pray again and put that verse in?" the girl asked. As he began, she called out, "Stop!
Let me put my finger on that verse."
The minister prayed. When he looked again, he saw hope and forgiveness and peace in the girl's face.
"I'm so glad God put in that word 'scarlet,'" she said. "That means me."
God will forgive every kind of sin.
So tell me, why won't you come when God says, "People will be forgiven for every kind of sin and blasphemy"?
Good heavens! I can't understand how you can just sit there.
But a man says, "Bill, will He forgive a murderer?
I have blood on my hands, even though no one knows it."
Didn't I tell you He forgave Paul?

blocks.x: A Forgiving God

s: A friend of mine was preaching in Lansing, Michigan, once. In the middle section of the church sat a man who made him so nervous that he couldn't look at him and preach.

Nothing seemed to catch the man's attention. Then my friend said, "Suppose there were a murderer here tonight. God would forgive him if he accepted Christ." At the word "murderer" the man grabbed the chair in front of him. He sat stiff for the rest of the sermon and never took his eyes off my friend.
At the end of the meeting my friend went down to him and asked what was wrong. He told him he had made him so nervous he could hardly preach.
The man said, "I'm a murderer.
I got off because of a technicality, and I'm supporting the widow and children. But I am a murderer."
My friend led him to Jesus Christ. Now that man is a strong force in the church.
God says He will forgive every kind of sin.
Some people say, "Mr. Sunday, why are so few old sinners converted?"
When unbelievers are asked this, they grab onto it as a way to attack.
When God begins to show His power, the devil and all the demons of hell get busy.
When that bunch of critics gets busy, it's the best proof in the world that these meetings are doing good.

Unbelievers sneer and say, "A man's mind grows through age and experience and contact with the world. He gets past the eager excitement of youth. So how is it that so few men like that are converted?"
Religion appeals to your feelings, not to your intellect.
You enter the kingdom of heaven heart first, not head first.
God is not an explanation. God is a revelation.
A grain of corn is a revelation, but you can't explain it.
You know that if you put something from the plant world into the soil, the plant will be born again. But you can't explain it.
Some of the greatest things are revelations.
So instead of being an argument against religion, it is an argument for it.
Don't you know that sixteen out of twenty people who are converted are converted before they turn twenty?
Don't you know that eighteen out of thirty who are converted are converted before they turn thirty?
Don't you know that?
What does that prove?
It proves this: if you are not converted before you are thirty, the chances are about 100,000 to one that you never will be.

blocks.x: The Power of Revivals

s: Most people are converted at special revival meetings.
I want to throw this in the teeth of those who sneer at revivals—preachers included. I want to cram it down their throats.
Almost nine out of ten Christians at this meeting were converted at a revival.
What does that show?
It shows this: if you are thirty and have not been converted, and you are not converted at this revival, you probably never will be.
Just think what hell would be like if there were no revivals.
Then think of any low-down, God-forsaken, dirty gang that attacks a revival.
God says, "You can reject My love and trample the blood under your feet. But if you ask for My pardon, I will forgive you."
You may have ignored the minister's appeals. You may have been a thief, or an adulterer, or a blasphemer, or a scoffer, and all that. But God says, "I will forgive you."
You may have ignored the tears of your poor wife and children and friends. But if you will seek God, He will forgive you.
But He came down and showed Himself to be the Son of God through the Holy Spirit. If you sneer and say it is not true, your sin may become unpardonable.
If you don't settle it here, you will never settle it anywhere else.
I will close with a word of comfort and a word of warning.
If you want to be a Christian, that proves the devil hasn't got you yet.
That is the comfort.
Now for the warning: if you have that desire, thank God for it and give in to it.
You may never have another chance.
"Lord, is it me?"—Matthew 26:22.

God made the first man and put him in the Garden of Eden. He gave him a clear command. But the man disobeyed, even though the warning about the punishment was still ringing in his ears. God had told him, "On the day you eat the fruit, you will surely die."
The Lord did not mean a period of twenty-four hours. He meant that man would reach a turning point in his life.
Adam ate the fruit God had forbidden, and this world became a graveyard.
If people had never sinned, we would never have died.
All the misery, all the sickness, and all the heartbreak have come because of sin.
The hearse backs up to our homes and drives away with the people we love. That happens because of sin.
But when man sinned, God made a promise: "The woman's child will crush the serpent's head."
When the right time came, Jesus came into the world to keep that promise.
He made blind people see. He calmed the storm. He fed a huge crowd with five loaves and two fish. He drove out demons, and He raised the dead.
By what He said and what He did, He showed that He was the Son of God.
The Jews turned their backs on His claim and rejected it. Their hatred kept growing until it finally led to His crucifixion.
But before that heartbreaking tragedy happened, several other things took place. I take my text from one of them.
Jesus said to His disciples, "Go into the village just ahead of you. You will find a colt, a young donkey, tied up there. No one has ever sat on him. Untie him and bring him to Me.
If anyone asks you why you are doing this, tell him, 'The Lord needs him.' Then he will send him here right away."

So the disciples went. They found the colt tied in front of a house where two roads met. A crowd of men was hanging around the place. If they were anything like the men of our day, they were whittling sticks, swearing, chewing tobacco, and arguing about money, politics, and every other public issue.
The disciples started to untie the colt. Then one fellow, who spits enough tobacco juice to drown a rabbit, shouts, "Hey there!
What are you doing?
What are you going to do with that colt?"
The disciples call back, "The Lord needs him."
So off they go with the colt to where Jesus was. Riding on its back, Jesus enters the city of Jerusalem. This is His famous triumphal entry.
A huge crowd followed, shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David!
Blessed is the One who comes in the Lord's name!"
They spread their coats on the ground in front of Jesus.
They cut branches from the trees. They covered His path with flowers.
From all their cheering, you would have thought they were going to make Him king right then and there. But let's wait and see.
Jesus said to Peter and John, "Go on ahead. You will meet a man carrying a jar of water.
Follow him into the house he goes into. Ask the owner of the house, 'Where is the guest room?'
He will show you an upstairs room with furniture in it. Get everything ready there."

Jesus wanted to eat the Passover meal with His disciples. This meal remembers the night the angel of death passed over. That angel went through the whole land of Egypt and killed the oldest son in every home that did not have blood on its doorposts.
That night at the table, Peter noticed that Jesus looked sad and troubled.
He turned to John, who was one of the disciples closest to Jesus, and said, "Ask Him what's wrong."
John said, "Master, you look worried.
Why?" Jesus answered, "One of you is going to betray Me."
Peter asked, in the words of my text, "Lord, is it me?"
John also asked, "Lord, is it me?"
And Judas, the worst traitor of all, had the nerve to look Jesus in the face and ask, "Lord, is it me?"

He asked this even though for days he had been bargaining over a price for betraying Jesus to the Pharisees. The price was thirty pieces of silver. That is about fifteen dollars and ninety-five cents in our money.
Jesus answered, "It is the one I give this piece of bread to."
Then He dipped the bread in the dish and handed it to Judas. He said, "Whatever you are going to do, do it fast."
Jesus' words cut Judas to the heart. He jumped to his feet. He was the treasurer of the little group of apostles, so he grabbed the money bag and left the room.
After they had sung a hymn, Jesus and the eleven disciples who were left went out. They crossed the Kidron stream and went into the Garden of Gethsemane.
This brings me to the subject of my sermon: The Three Groups in the Garden.

blocks.x: I. They Stood in Different Places

s: They were not put into groups by how much money they had, the way credit agencies like Bradstreet or Dun rate people.
Each man chose his own group. And you do the same.
You are where you are because Jesus knows He cannot trust you with a more important place.
Judas put himself on the side of God's enemies.
The first group was near the edge of the garden. The second group was farther in. And Jesus, we are told, was a stone's throw beyond them.
The first group of disciples was so close to the edge that they only had a short way to go to be outside. That is where Judas was, with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the mob.
I am sorry to say it, but it's the truth.
The truth is not always nice to hear. But it does good to everyone who is willing to learn from it.
The first group is like a large share of the members in the average church today.

They live selfish, careless, half-hearted lives. They want to stay on good terms with both God and the devil. Their lives are like milk mixed with chalk, or cider turning to vinegar. It is hard to tell whether they belong to the church or to the world.
I can't stand a man who changes course just to catch a little breeze of popularity, and who fights under a flag no one can be sure of.
I love to see a person come out completely on God's side, with no compromise.
The closer the relationship, the more we owe.
I owe my wife, Mrs. Sunday, and our children something I do not owe any other woman or children in the world. That is because of how closely I am tied to them.
You owe your wife and children something you do not owe anyone else.
I owe Jesus something I do not owe the world.
I speak out about the world and say that what it does is evil.
I don't care whether people boo me or cheer me. I don't care whether they invite me to dinner or curse me.
Jesus said, "The world will hate you just as it hates Me."
"How terrible for you when everyone says good things about you."
One of the worst things anyone could say at your funeral is that you had no enemies.
If you live for Christ without compromise, you will have enemies.
The closer the relationship, the more deeply we can hurt someone.
With one act I could break my wife's heart and bring shame on my children. But that same act would not bring a single tear to your eye.
Why? Because you are only interested in me so I can entertain you or teach you. Maybe your concern for me stops there.
I have often thought that the way so many church people behave must almost break Christ's heart.

God has every right to say, "I did not send My Son into the world to soak it in blood and tears, and to have His veins opened by the cruel cross, just so He could rescue you to serve your selfish desires and the devil. I sent Him so you would serve Me.
I want your influence, your time, your money, your prayers, and your tears."
Someone once asked Alexander the Great to compete in the Olympic Games.
He answered, "I will, if the other runners on the track are kings."
We have been born again from above. If we did nothing in this world that didn't fit that new birth, we would move this sin-soaked old world toward God.
You cannot just do whatever you like.
The higher you climb, the more easily people can see you.
When you are away from home, don't forget that God is everywhere.

The son of a Roman named Fulvius was caught with Catiline and his fellow plotters. His old father scolded him, saying, "I did not bring you into the world to serve Catiline. I did it so you would serve your country—Rome!"
You have been bought back by the precious blood of Christ. It was not so you would serve the world, but so you would serve God.

I love to see people as loyal to Jesus as Speaker Lenthall was to the Constitution in the days of King Charles I. When he was ordered to shut down Parliament, he said, "I have no eyes to see, no ears to hear, and no tongue to speak, except as the Constitution directs me. I am its servant."
Or I love to see them as loyal as Prince William of Orange was to the Netherlands during the thirty-seven years of war.
King Philip of Spain offered him huge amounts of money to give up.

Prince William sent back a message that is now set deep in the hearts of the Dutch people like a mosaic: "Not for my life, not for my wife, not for my children, and not for land would I put one drop of the poison of treason into my cup!"
No wonder that when a murderer killed him, little children stopped playing and cried.
Many of our churches are hardly more than social clubs.
They spend more time growing their social life than their spiritual life.
Businessmen and important church members do not do their duty. They are completely caught up in their own business.
They are busy chasing the things and the silly fun of the world, and they lose their way.
The fire and the spirit of the old days are missing.
What else can we expect from a social club, except that it will lead people away from God?
Our churches need more of God. They need less of fancy clothes, less chasing after money, and less social life.
A woman in a city out West went to her pastor and asked, "What can I do to win my husband to Christ?"
He answered, "The way you live, you can't win anyone to Christ."
She hung her head in shame and went home.
When her husband and her eighteen-year-old son came home, she said to them, "Please stay a little while after dinner.
I want to talk with you."

They went into the living room. She put an arm around each of them and said, "I have not lived like a real Christian should. So I feel I have not been as good a wife to you, my husband, or as good a mother to you, my son, as I should have been.
Will you pray with me that God will forgive me?"
All three of them knelt down. She tried to pray, but all she could say was, "O God!
O God!" But the Holy Spirit broke their hearts wide open like a flood, and all three of them cried.
A few days later her husband openly accepted Christ and joined the church.

She asked, "Husband, tell me, why couldn't I win you to Christ before?" He said, "I would ask you to go to the theater with me, and you would go. I'd ask you to go to the dance, and you would go. I'd ask you to play cards, and you would.
You drank wine with me.
Then you would ask me to go to church with you, and to the prayer meeting, and I would go.
You went where I went, and I went where you went.
You did what I did, and I did what you did.
So how was your life any better than mine?"
If we want to help others see their sin, we must first get right with God ourselves.

blocks.x: II. The Groups Were Different Sizes

s: There were eight in the first group.
There were three in the second group.
Jesus alone made up the third.
The biggest number was in the first group.
They were the farthest from Jesus. They were the closest to the world.
That has always been true of every church I have known anything about.
Ask the minister for a list of his members. Then sit down and check off the ones who come to prayer meeting.
You will find that most of them are closer to the card party and the wine supper. They are closer to the world than to the cross of Christ.
When Daniel Webster was a boy, someone asked him, "What are you going to be when you grow up?"
"A lawyer," he answered.
"But there are already too many lawyers."
Webster answered, "There is plenty of room at the top."
The closer you get to Jesus, the more room you will have, and the smaller the crowd.
The greatest things people do are not always the clearest sign of what is bad or good in them.

Sometimes a single word, an action, or a gesture tells more. Whether you show up or stay away can show more clearly what kind of man or woman you are, or whether you are much of one at all, than some brave or daring deed.
Let's talk with Jesus for a minute.
"Jesus, how many disciples do you have?"
"I had twelve. Now I have only eleven."
"Where is the missing one?"
"He has gone to betray Me."
"And even with eleven left, you are praying all alone?"
That is just like many ministers. They have hundreds of members, yet they carry the load all alone.
Judas bought a ticket to hell for thirty pieces of silver. And it wasn't a round-trip ticket either.
Let's go and talk with the eight:
"Where is Jesus?" "We don't know."
"Where are Peter, James, and John?"
"We don't know. We haven't seen them."
"Where is Judas?" "Why, he just went by a little while ago, with the scribes and Pharisees and a big crowd."
"Where was he going?"
"Well, he was looking for Jesus so he could betray Him."
"Why do you think that?"
"Because tonight at the meal Jesus said, 'One of you is going to betray Me. It is the one I give this piece of bread to.' Then He dipped it in the dish and handed it to Judas."
"Didn't you try to stop him from doing such a wicked thing as betraying Jesus?"
"No." "Well, don't you think Judas expected to find Jesus here with you men?"
No, he never imagined that Jesus would be anywhere near that bunch.
Judas knew that crowd.
He knew that first group near the edge of the garden inside and out.
Why do I think so?
I'll tell you.

Jesus had gone up the mountain where He was transfigured. He took Peter, James, and John with Him, the men of the second group. While He was gone, a father came to the disciples of the first group, the ones near the edge of the garden. His boy had a demon in him. The father begged them to drive the demon out of his son.

Jesus had given His disciples power over evil spirits so they could drive them out. But instead of doing the work He gave them, they spent their time arguing about who would be the greatest in the kingdom.
I wonder if there is any father in the world who has never had trouble with his boy.
This father was weighed down with trouble, and the devil had caused all of it.
The devil is behind every saloon, every drunk, every murder, every theft, every lie, every heartache, and every house of prostitution.
All the lies, jealousy, hatred, and dirty talk that come out of your mouth are stirred up by the devil. And yet some people think I am throwing stones at them when I preach against the devil.
Some people say, "Well, the devil brings in money, so let him stay.
We need the license fees from the saloons to pave our streets and light our city."
Yes, and you need your saloons to keep your jails, prisons, poorhouses, and mental hospitals full.
Every saloon gives the devil that much better a chance to get your boy.
If you want the world to be better someday, keep the devil out of the boys and girls.
If you want to drive the devil out of the world, fight him at the cradle, not when people already need a crutch.
When Jesus came back down from the mountain, the heartbroken father ran to Him with his boy. He cried, "If You can do anything, have pity on us and help us.
I brought my son to Your disciples, and they could not drive the demon out!"
That word "if" shows he had doubts.
Those disciples had not stayed close to Jesus, so they did not have the power to drive out demons. Their failure made the poor old father doubt Jesus' power.
The way thousands of church members live out God's teaching turns more people into unbelievers than all the Paines, Parkers, and Ingersolls put together.
The more a standard really means, the fewer people there are who should be counted as keeping it.
Suppose that by "educated" I mean everyone who can read and write. Then there are about eighty-five million educated people in the United States.
But suppose by "educated" I mean everyone who has finished high school. Then only about one out of five people would count as educated.
And if by "educated" I mean everyone who has graduated from a university or college, only one-half of one percent would fit.
Suppose that by your friends you mean everyone who shakes your hand, smiles, and says, "How are you?
I'm glad to see you."

You have lots of friends like that. But suppose by friends you mean the people who will stick with you no matter what, and stand up for you when they hear someone say bad things about you. I'm afraid there are very few of those.
Suppose that by a Christian I mean everyone whose name is on a church list. There are about twenty-six million of them in the United States, split about evenly between Catholics and Protestants.
But suppose I mean every man and woman who is willing to do what God wants. I doubt that there are ten million who would die for Jesus.
One time I asked a minister, "How many members do you have?"
He said, "Eight hundred seventy-two. But there are two hundred seventy-eight that I don't count."
I asked, "Of the ones you do count, how many are helping in the meetings? How many sing in the choir, work as ushers, or talk to people one-on-one about Christ?"
Tears ran down his cheeks as he said, "The most I have ever been able to gather on any one night was twenty-eight. If my life depended on getting fifty, I would die!"

There we were, wearing ourselves out trying to bring that town to its knees. It was a godless town, soaked in whiskey, cursed by gambling, and ruined by prostitution. And the church just sat there calmly and watched.
Sometimes I wonder if the church needs new members even half as much as it needs the old members to be made over new.

From the way so many church people live, you would think they believe they have a first-class ticket straight through to heaven in a luxury sleeping car. You would think they have told the porter to wake them up when the train pulls into the station at the New Jerusalem.
If that's what you think, you are going to be disappointed. Your car will overheat and be pulled off onto a side track.

Suppose I had a hundred tongues, each one speaking a different language in a different key, all at the same time. I still could not describe the grand mess that a certain crowd in the church brings to the cause of Christ. They love the world, they dance, they play cards, they guzzle whiskey, they fizz with gin and sizzle with wine, and they read novels.
Faithful preachers and workers all say the same thing about the church: "She is sick." But we say it so gently and softly that she seems to enjoy being sick.
About four out of every five people whose names are on our church lists are doing nothing to bring the world to Christ. The church is not one bit better because they are in it.
To make up for all this, Christians are making a big deal out of Lent.
I believe in a Lent that lasts all three hundred sixty-five days of the year.
I think it makes a mockery of Christ's teaching when people think they can store up so much holiness in forty days that they can live like the devil the rest of the year.
That is an old trick of the devil.
The Jewish church hit that rock and was wrecked.
The Roman Catholic church hit it and was split apart.
The Protestant church is quickly heading for the same end.

As I see it, these are some of the great dangers: becoming just like the world, ignoring the poor, putting outward religious forms in place of real godliness, and having ministers who only work for pay. Add it all up, and you get a fashionable church with the religion left out.
Methodists used to go to their class meetings and share their testimonies. Now class meetings are a thing of the past.
People used to shout their praise to God.
Now that kind of holy excitement is thought to be undignified.
Every now and then some godly old woman, a sort of link between the old days and the new, pipes up. In a weak, timid, high-pitched, apologetic little voice, she says:
"Amen, Brother Sunday!"

I don't expect any of these stiff, stone-hard, moldy Presbyterians or Episcopalians to shout "Amen!"—the kind who are dyed-in-the-wool, stamped on the cork and blown in the bottle, set in their ways from every direction. But it would do you good to loosen up.
Many of you are stuck in your narrow ways.
I believe that half of the people who say they are Christians are worth nothing as a spiritual force.

They go to church, and they think kindly of religion. But when it comes to holding on tight to God, cheerfully giving things up, serving with excitement, praying prayers that get answers, and being willing to hit the devil with hard, staggering blows, they are nearly failures.
Someone has invented a shell that puts everyone on a ship to sleep when it hits.
Something like that seems to have hit our churches.

blocks.x: III. Jesus Revealed Different Things to Each

s: Jesus spoke to the first group, the biggest one, near the edge of the garden. He said, "Sit here."
To the second group He said, "My heart is so heavy with sorrow that I feel I could die.
Wait here and stay awake with Me.
Stay awake and pray, so that you will not fall when you are tempted.
Your spirit truly wants to do what is right, but your human nature is weak."
But when He was alone, He cried out, "Father, if there is any way, let this cup pass by Me. But not My will—let Your will be done."
Notice how He revealed more and more, step by step.
Not a word to Judas.
To the eight who were closest to the world, He said, "Sit here."
To Peter, James, and John, He said, "Stay awake and pray."
When He was alone with the Father, He said, "Your will be done."
He told the Father things He did not tell Peter, James, and John.
He told those three things He did not tell the group of eight, and did not tell Judas.
Do you want God to show you the deep things of the Spirit?
Then turn your back on sinful things and stay close by His side.
Jesus will never show you His secrets while you are standing at a bar drinking, or at a baseball game on the Sabbath, or living in sin.
Jesus did not ask the people in the first group, near the edge of the garden, to pray.
Maybe they would have said no.
Every minister knows there are certain members of his church he would never think of asking to lead in prayer.
In fact, they never set foot in a prayer meeting. If there is a card party on prayer meeting night, that is where they are.
And yet we wonder why this sin-ruined old world is not on its knees.
I am amazed that God is doing as well as He is with the crowd He has to work with.
Please excuse me for talking about myself. I was born and raised, not in Old Kentucky, though my grandfather was born in Lexington, but in Old Iowa.
I was the biggest country bumpkin of them all, a hayseed through and through.
I have greased my hair with goose fat.
I have shined my boots with stove polish.
I have wiped my face on a towel made from a burlap sack.
I have eaten with my knife.
I have drunk coffee out of my saucer.
I have said "done it" when I should have said "did it," "came" when I should have said "come," and "seen" when I should have said "saw."
I graduated from the school of being poor and having a hard life, and I have taken the advanced courses too.
The story of my life could be summed up in one line from Gray's poem "Elegy": "The short and simple story of the poor."
My father joined the army four months before I was born.
He went off to war with Company E of the Twenty-third Iowa Infantry, but he never came back.
He died and was buried at Camp Patterson, Missouri.
I have had to fight my way through life since I was six years old.
I know all about the dark and ugly side of life.
If any man ever had to fight hard for every inch of his way, I did.
One day Mother said, "Boys, I am going to send you to the Soldiers' Orphans' Home in Glenwood, Iowa."
We had to go to Ames to catch the train.
We went to a little hotel to wait. At about one o'clock someone came and said, "Get ready for the train. It's coming."
I looked at Mother's face.
Her eyes were red, and her hair was a mess.
I said, "What's wrong, Mother?"
The whole time Ed and I were asleep, Mother had been praying.
We went to the train.
Mother put one arm around me and the other around Ed. She sobbed as if her heart would break.
People walked by and looked at us, but they didn't say a word.
Why? They didn't know. And even if they had known, they wouldn't have cared.
Mother knew. She knew she would not see her boys for years.
We got on the train, and as it pulled away we cried, "Goodbye, Mother!"
We got to Council Bluffs.
It was cold. We turned up the collars of our thin little coats around our necks and shivered.
We saw a hotel. We went up and asked a woman for something to eat.
She said, "What's your name?"
"My name is Willie Sunday, and this is my brother Ed," I said.
"Where are you going?"
"We're going to the Soldiers' Orphans' Home at Glenwood."
She wiped away her tears and said, "My husband was a soldier, and he never came back.
He would never turn anyone away, and I certainly won't turn you boys away."
She threw her arms around us and said, "Come on in."
She gave us breakfast, and our midday meal too.
There was no train leaving on the Burlington line until the afternoon.
We played around the railroad yards.
We saw a freight train standing there, so we climbed into the caboose.
The conductor came along and said, "Where is your money?"
"Don't have any." "Where are your tickets?"
"Don't have any." "You can't ride without money or tickets.
I'll have to put you off the train."
We started to cry.
My brother handed him a letter introducing us to the director of the Orphans' Home.
The conductor read it. Tears were rolling down his cheeks as he handed it back. Then he said, "Just sit still, boys.
It won't cost you a penny to ride on my train."
It's only twenty miles from Council Bluffs to Glenwood. As we came around the curve, the conductor said, "There's the Home on the hill."
Mother knew. Ed didn't know.
I didn't know. I went to sleep.
So did Ed. But Mother knew. She prayed.
Jesus knew. He prayed.
Peter, James, and John went to sleep.
You can't make me believe that you would act the way you do if you really knew.
Tell me how much you read the Bible, how much you pray, and how much you do to help people come to Jesus Christ. Then I will tell you where you stand on the spiritual thermometer.

The trouble is this. You will be in church on Sunday morning. You will keep a little spot about eighteen inches square warm for half an hour. You will listen to the sermon. Then you will pick up a hymnbook and sing "Jesus Paid It All," while you have debts so old that the law can no longer make you pay them.
He doesn't pay them.
He doesn't pay for that hat, or for that set of false teeth you are wearing.
You stand up and say, "I am standing on the solid rock."
