You are probably standing in a pair of shoes you haven't paid for yet.
Let's get our lives cleaned up for God, and see if the Lord won't do great things.
He will not send the wind to push our ships along unless we have enough faith to raise our sails.

blocks.x: IV. Each Group Had a Different Duty

s: To the people in the first group, Jesus said, "Sit here."
To the second group He said, "Stay awake and pray."
His own duty was to carry the sins of the world. Yet there are crowds of people in the church who do nothing.
They are just zeros.
Once a preacher did not show up for a funeral.
The funeral director thought it would be a real shame to bury the man without anyone saying something. So he decided to say a few words himself.
When the time came, he cleared his throat and said in a whiny, holy-sounding voice, "Dear friends, this corpse has been a member of this church for forty years!"
"Crucify Him!" shouted the merciless mob.
The yelling of that furious crowd shook the temple from its foundation to the tops of its towers.
People had often seen crowds full of this kind of hatred when citizens fought among themselves.
It truly seemed as if all the ghosts of hell had gathered in Jerusalem. The mob poured out through the funeral gate.
Here comes Judas, leading the devil's crowd.
He turned to the Pharisees and said, "The man I kiss is the one you want. Grab Him and hold on to Him."
Look at the smile on his two-faced, falsely holy face as he rushes forward shouting, "Greetings, Master!" and kisses Him.
Jesus answers, "Judas, are you using a kiss to betray the Son of Man?"
They grab Him and take Him to the High Priest's house. There, based on lies, He is sentenced to die on a cross like a criminal.

blocks.x:
"Must Jesus carry the cross alone,
While all the world goes free?
No! There's a cross for everyone,
And there's a cross for me."

s: Someone once described the scene beautifully. He imagined that if we had been there, and God had let us see it, we might have seen the hilltops covered with angels and the sky filled with the armies of heaven. They were all watching that scene and holding their breath.
The archangel opened the door of heaven and cried out:
"O Jesus! If you want me to come and help you, lift your head and look this way. I will come with a whole army of angels to help you!"
But Jesus kept on suffering.
He pictured the archangel leaning over the walls of heaven once more and crying out again, with a voice that shook the earth:
"O Jesus, Son of God!
If you want me to come and throw that howling, bloodthirsty mob into hell, pull your right hand free from the cross and wave it!"
But Jesus closed His fingers tight over the nails in His hands and kept on suffering.
Why? To open up a way to be saved. If we accept it, it will keep us out of hell.
Suddenly He cried out, "It is finished!" Then the Holy Spirit picked the olive branch of peace from the cross. He flew back and burst through the gates of glory, shouting, "Peace!
Peace! Peace! It has been made through His death on the cross."
How many will stay with Jesus to the very end?
Thousands will. But many people are like the disciples. They follow Him to the Garden, but they leave Him at the Cross.
How many will say with Jesus, "Not my will, but Yours be done"?
Say it with me: "Not my will, but——" Now finish the sentence.
All the peace, all the power, all the blessing of the Christian life, and joy that lasts forever are found in the three words you left out: "Yours be done."
For some people, saying "Yours be done" costs too much.
One person says, "If I say that, the saloon owners won't shop at my store anymore.
If I said that, I would have to close my store on the Sabbath."
"If I said that, I couldn't accept Mrs. So-and-So's invitation to a card party."
"If I said that, I would have to pay my debts."
"If I said that, I would have to go home and burn the prizes I've won playing progressive euchre."
"If I said that, I couldn't go to the brothel anymore and crawl into the arms of shame."
"If I said, 'Your will be done,' I would have to pour the wine out of my cellar and smash my beer bottles.
I'm going to have a few bottles with dinner tonight."
"If I said that, I couldn't go to the ball game on Sunday afternoon."
"If I said that, I would have to stop telling lies about my neighbors."
Oh yes, saying "Yours be done" costs too much.
That is why you lose out.
That is why your morals have a crooked backbone.
That is why your spiritual batting average doesn't measure up to the standard of God's league.
"Not my will, but——" That's where you quit the game.
That's where you drive into the ditch.
That's where you turn off the light.
That's where you hang up the phone.
That's where you cut off the call.
That's where you get a flat tire.
That's where you strike out.
Saying "Yours be done" costs too much.
"Hey, Dad, can I go with you?" a little boy asked his father.
"Yes, son, come on," said the father. He threw the ax over his shoulder, and he and a friend went to the woods and cut down a tree.
The little boy said:
"Hey, Dad, can I go and play in the water in the lagoon?"
"Yes, but be careful. Don't go into the deep water. Stay close to the shore."
The little boy was playing. He was digging holes, picking up stones and shells, and talking to himself. Then all of a sudden the father heard him cry:
"Hurry, Dad, hurry!"
The father jumped up, grabbed the ax, and ran to the lagoon. He saw the boy struggling in deep water. His hands were stretched out, and his face was full of terror as he cried:
"Hurry, Dad, hurry! The alligator has got me!"
The ugly monster had been sleeping through the winter. It had come out thin, bony, and starving, and it grabbed the boy.

The father jumped into the lagoon. He was just about to bring the ax down on the monster's head when it turned. It whipped the water with its huge tail like the propeller of an ocean ship. And the little boy cried out:
"Hurry, Dad, hurry!"
The foam, speckled with blood, told the story.
When I read that, I could not eat for days, and I could not sleep for nights. I said:
"O God, what if that had been my boy!"
There are forces in this world worse than an alligator. They are ripping and tearing our goodness and our morals to shreds.
Some young men are trapped by drinking; others by other sins.
Drunkards are crying out to the church, "Hurry faster!" And the church members sit on the shore playing cards. They sit there drinking beer and reading novels.
"Hurry!"
They argue over tiny, silly things instead of trying to keep sinners out of hell!
"Faster! Faster! Faster!"
"Lord, is it me?"
Our bodies live and grow strong through exercise.
We are saved by faith. But we must work out our salvation by doing what God wants.
The more we do for God, the more God will do through us.
Faith grows through experience.
If you are a stranger to prayer, you are a stranger to the greatest source of power people know.
Suppose we took care of our bodies in the same careless way we take care of our spiritual life. Then we would be as weak in body as we are in spirit.
Week after week you go without praying.
I want to be a giant for God.
You don't even sing. You let the choir do it.
You go to the prayer meeting and never give a testimony.
You are a stranger to the great privilege that is offered to people.
Some of the greatest blessings people enjoy come from prayer.
When you pray earnestly, you think the way the Lord leads you, and you lose yourself in him.
Some people say, "There's no point in praying.
The Lord knows everything anyway."
That's true. He does.
He is not limited the way I am.
He knows everything, and he has known it since before the world began.
We don't know everyone who will be converted at this revival. But that doesn't free us from our duty.
We don't know, and we still must do the work he has commanded us to do.
Others say, "But I don't get what I pray for."
Well, everything has a cause.
Find the cause, and you'll be all right.
When you are sick and call the doctor, he doesn't pay attention to the sickness itself. He looks at what caused it.
If you have a headache, don't rub your forehead.
In Matthew it says, "Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you."
If your prayers are not answered, you are not right with God.
If you have no faith, or if your reason for praying is wrong, then your prayers will be useless.
Often when people pray, they are being selfish.
They are not holding on to the word.

Many a wife prays for her husband to be converted. But I believe it is often not because she really wants his soul to be saved. It's because she thinks life would be easier for her if he were converted.
Pray for your neighbors, not just for your own family.
The pastor of one church does not pray for the people of a church from another denomination.
I'm not saying anything against denominations.
I believe in them.
I believe they come from God.
Different denominations stand for different temperaments.
A man with warm feelings would not make a good Episcopalian. But he would make a first-rate Methodist.
Oh, what a curse selfishness is!
The church is dying for religion—pure religion, with no stain on it.
Pure religion, with no stain on it, means visiting widows and orphans. It means doing God's will without thinking so much about yourself.
I tell you, a lot of people are going to be fooled on Judgment Day.
Isaiah says that God's hand is not too short and his ear is not deaf.
No, his hand is not too short to save.
He has provided ways for us to be saved.
If he had made no way for you to be saved, then the problem would be with God. But he has. So if you go to hell, the problem will be with you.
In Ezekiel we read that people have taken idols into their hearts and put stumbling blocks in front of their faces.
God will not hear you if you put clothes, money, or pride in your family connections ahead of him.
You know there is sin in your life.
Many people know there is sin in their lives, but they still ask God to bless them.
They should first get down on their knees and pray, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner."
Some people are so shamefully stingy that God won't hear them.
God won't hear you if you close your ears to the cries of the poor.
You drag along here for three weeks and raise a tiny amount of money. A circus would take that much out of town in two hours.
When they give things to the poor, they rip off the buttons and the fine trim.
Some people pick out old clothes that moths have eaten full of holes. They give them to the poor and think they are being generous.
That isn't charity, no sir! It's charity when you give something you will miss.
It's charity when you feel it as you give.
And when you stand to pray, forgive anyone you have something against.
There is no point in praying if you have a mean, nasty attitude. It's no use if you are grumpy, or if you quarrel at home or with your neighbors.
There's no point in praying for a blessing while you are feuding with your neighbors.
It doesn't do you any good.
You go to a sewing circle to make mosquito nets for the Eskimos and blankets for the Hottentots. But instead you sit and gossip and tear some woman apart behind her back.
The Spirit of God runs away from fighting and quarreling.
People say, "She is a good woman, but a worldly Christian."
What? You might as well talk about a heavenly devil!
You could just as well expect a mummy to talk and have babies as expect that kind of person to move the world toward God.
Prayer brings you closer to God.

blocks.x: Learning from Christ

s: When we say, "Teach us to pray," it means I want to be taught.
It's a great privilege to be taught by Jesus.
A friend of mine was preaching in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. He had to go to a hospital in Chicago for an operation, so I was asked to go and preach in his place.
Alexander was leading the singing. One night Charles called a little girl out of the audience to sing.
She didn't look older than four or five, though she might have been a bit older.
I thought, "What's the point?
No one will ever hear her little voice over this crowd."
But Charlie stood her on a chair next to the pulpit. She threw back her head, and out came some of the sweetest music I have ever heard.
It was wonderful. I sat there with tears streaming down my cheeks.
That little girl's father was an engineer on the Northwestern railroad. He took her to Chicago when her mother was away.
Someone took her to Patti.
Patti took the little girl into one room of her suite and told her to stand there and sing.
Then Patti went to the other end of the suite, sat down on a couch, and listened.
The song moved her to tears.
She ran over and hugged and kissed the little girl. She sat her down on the couch and said, "Now you sit here, and I'll go over there and sing."
She stood where the child had stood. Then she lifted her magnificent voice and sang "Home, Sweet Home" and "The Last Rose of Summer." She sang them for that little girl!
And Patti used to get a thousand dollars for one song, too!
She always knew how many songs she was supposed to sing, because she got a check before she went on stage.
That little daughter of the railroad engineer had a great privilege. But it's an even greater privilege to learn from Jesus Christ how to pray.

A friend told me he went to hear Paganini play. The great violinist broke one string on his violin, then another, then another, until only one was left. And on that one string he played so wonderfully that the audience burst into thunderous applause.
It was a privilege to hear that. But it's a greater privilege to have Jesus teach you to pray.
Let's look at a few examples from Christ's life.
Mark tells us that Jesus got up early in the morning, went out to a lonely place, and prayed.
He started every day with prayer.
You never get up without getting dressed.
You never forget to wash your face and comb your hair.
You always think of breakfast.
You feed your body.
So why do you starve your spiritual body?
If nine out of ten of you were as weak in body as you are in spirit, you couldn't even walk.
When I was assistant secretary of the YMCA in Chicago, John G. Paton came home from the New Hebrides. He was giving lectures and collecting money.

He was raising money to buy a steam yacht that could sail the open sea. His work took him from island to island, and he had to use a rowboat. That was sometimes dangerous in bad weather, so he wanted the yacht.
He was with us for a week, and I had the privilege of going to lunch with him.
We would go out to a restaurant at noon, and he would talk to us.

Sometimes there were as many as fifteen or twenty preachers in the group. Now and then some of us got so caught up in what he told us about the work for Jesus on those faraway islands that we forgot to eat.
I remember one day he said, "I owe everything I am to my Christian father and mother.
My father was one of the most prayerful men I have ever known.

Often during the day he would slip into his little room. He would drop a handkerchief outside the door. When we children saw that white guard, we knew Father was talking with his God, and we would quietly go away.
I am preaching to the cannibals in the South Seas largely because of the life and influence of that same godly father."
It is an insult to God and a disgrace to let children grow up without surrounding them with Christian influence.
Seven out of ten people who say they are Christians have no family prayers and do not read the Bible.
No wonder boys and girls are going to hell.
No wonder the cursed ballrooms are ruining the virtue of our girls.
Matthew chapter fourteen tells us that after Jesus had sent the crowds away, he went up on the mountain and was there alone with God.
Jesus Christ never forgot to thank God for answering his prayers.
Jesus asked God to help him feed the crowd, and he didn't fail to thank him for it.
Next time you pray, don't ask God for anything.
Just try to think of all the things you have to be thankful for, and tell him about them.

blocks.x: Pride Gets in the Way of Prayer

s: Pride keeps us from praying the right way.
Being stuck-up and big-headed causes more failures than anything else in the world.
It has spoiled many preachers, just as it has spoiled many workers.
Some fellows get a job, and in about two weeks they think they know more about the business than the boss.
They think he is all wrong.
It never occurs to them that it took brains and know-how to build that business and keep it running until they came along.
Here are two things to watch out for.
Don't get proud when you succeed, and don't get discouraged when you seem to fail.
"And when he prayed, he said, 'Lazarus, come out!' And the man who had been dead came out."
If we prayed the right way, we would raise people out of sin and bring them out into the light of righteousness.
"And as he prayed, the look on his face changed."
Ladies, do you want to look pretty?
Some of you women should spend less on beauty lotions and cold cream, and get down on your knees and pray. Then God would make you prettier.
Why, I can look at your faces and tell what kind of lives you live.
If you give all your time and thoughts to high society, your faces will show it.
If you pray, I can see that.
Every man who has helped bring light to the dark places of the world has been a man of prayer.
I never preach a sermon until I have soaked it in prayer.
Never. And then I never forget to thank God for helping me preach.
I don't care whether you read your prayers from a book or just say them, as long as you mean them.
A man can read his prayers and go to heaven. Or he can just say his prayers and go to hell.
We have to face the facts.
When I read, I find that all the godly men who got things done, from Pentecost until today, knew how to pray.
It was a master stroke of the devil when he got the church to give up prayer.
One of the biggest jokes today is the average prayer meeting.

blocks.x: Praying in Secret

s: Matthew says, "But when you pray, go into your room and shut your door. Pray to your Father, who is in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you openly."
Two men came to the Temple to pray. The first was the Pharisee.
He was nice and smooth, and his attitude was nice and smooth too.
He prayed, "God, I thank you that I am not like other people—cheats, crooks, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week, and I give a tenth of all I own." And he went out.
I can picture a lot of people sitting around the church saying, "That's my idea of religion. That's it.
I don't like sensational preaching. I don't want anything vulgar, no slang."
Why don't you use a little of it, buddy, so that something will come your way?
And it will come as surely as two plus two make four.
When people serve in such opposite ways, they cannot get the same results.
Suppose two men were on top of a tall building. One jumps off, and the other comes down the fire escape. They can't expect to be equally safe!
The Pharisee said, "Thank God I am not like other people." And the tax collector said, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner."
The first man went home the same as he was when he left.
"God, be merciful to me, a sinner."
That man was made right with God.
I am made right with God through my faith in Jesus Christ.
I am not a sinner anymore.
Through faith in the Son of God I am made right with God, just as if I had never sinned.
That man went home made right with God.

blocks.x: Praying Humbly

s: How many people really pray?
How many people pray humbly and truly?
Some men pray for humility when what they really want is pride.
Many a man kneels down and says, "Our Father, who is in heaven, may your name be honored as holy. May your kingdom come—" But that isn't true. They don't want God's kingdom to come.
It isn't true for half the people who pray.
I tell you, when you pray that in the church pew, it doesn't count for a snap of my fingers if you don't live it.
You pray, "May your kingdom come," and then you go out and do something that keeps that kingdom from coming.
No man can kneel and pray "May your kingdom come" and then have a beer wagon back up to his door and put beer in the icebox.
No man can get down on his knees and pray "May your kingdom come" and then look through the bottom of a beer glass.
God won't put up with it.
If you wanted God's will to be done, you would do God's will, even if it took every drop of blood in your body.
"May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven."
When you say this in your pew on Sunday, it means nothing unless you live it on Monday.
You say "May your kingdom come," and then go out and do the very thing that will keep God's kingdom from coming.
Your prayers, and everything you do in church on Sunday, mean nothing if you don't do the same in business on Monday.
I don't care how loud you blow hot air in prayer meeting if you go out the next day and cheat somebody in a horse deal.
The man who truly prays "May your kingdom come" can't take his heart out of his prayer when he is out of the church.
The man who truly prays "May your kingdom come" won't give short measure at his store. The load of coal he sends you won't be half slate.
The man who truly prays "May your kingdom come" won't cut off his yardstick when he measures you a piece of calico.

A man who truly prays "May your kingdom come" won't need the pure-food law to stop him. He won't put chalk in the flour, sand in the sugar, brick dust in the red pepper, or ground peanut shells in the breakfast food.

The man who truly prays "May your kingdom come" can't walk past a saloon without asking himself, "What can I do to get rid of that thing? It is ruining the lives of thousands of young men. It is wrecking homes. It is dragging men and women down to hell."
You can't pray "May your kingdom come" and then rush to the polls and vote for the thing that keeps that kingdom from coming.
You can't pray "May your kingdom come" and then go and do the things that make the devil laugh.
If a man truly prays "May your kingdom come," he can't have one kind of religion on his knees and another behind the counter. He can't have one kind of religion in the pew and another in politics.
When a man truly prays "May your kingdom come," he means it in everything, or he means it in nothing.
A lot of church members are praying the wrong way.
First you should pray, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner." Then pray, "May your kingdom come."
Saying a prayer is one thing. Doing God's will is another.
The two should mean the same thing.
Angels are angels because they do God's will.
When they refuse to do God's will, they become devils.
Many a man prays when he gets into a jam.
Many a man prays when he is up against it.
Many a man prays in times of trouble. But when he can stick his thumbs in the armholes of his vest and take a pair of scissors to clip his coupons, then it's "Goodbye, God. I'll see you later."
Many a man makes promises to God when he is desperate, but forgets them when he is doing well.
Many a man makes promises to God when the hearse is backed up to the door to carry the baby out. But he soon forgets the promises he made in those hard days.
Many a man makes promises while he lies on his back, thinking he is going to die. But once he is on his feet again, he loads up on drink just the same.

blocks.x: Men of Prayer

s: Every man and every woman God has used to stop this sin-cursed world and turn it toward God has been a praying Christian.
Martin Luther got up from his bed and prayed all night. When day broke, he called his wife and said to her, "It has come."
History tells us that on that very day King Charles granted religious toleration, the very thing Luther had prayed for.
John Knox's queen feared him more than any other man. He was in such agony of prayer that he ran out into the street, fell on his face, and cried, "O God, give me Scotland or I'll die."
And God gave him Scotland. And not only that—he threw in England for good measure.

Jonathan Edwards was about to preach his greatest sermon, "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God." Before he did, he prayed for days. When he stood before the congregation and preached it, men grabbed the seats in terror, and some fell to the floor. The people cried out in fear, "Mr. Edwards, tell us how we can be saved!"
The critical period of American history was between 1784 and 1789.
There was no shared money and no shared defense.

The colonies sent men to a convention to write a constitution. Benjamin Franklin stood up, carrying the weight of his eighty years, and asked that the convention begin with prayer. And there George Washington sealed the deal with God.
That winter at Valley Forge, Washington led his men in prayer, and he got down on his knees to do it.
During the battle of Gettysburg, Lincoln—old Abe Lincoln—was on his knees before God. Yes, he was on his knees from five in the afternoon until four in the morning, and Bishop Simpson was with him.
"And whatever you ask the Father in my name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son."
No one can ever be saved without Jesus Christ.
There is no way to God except through Jesus Christ.
It's Jesus Christ or nothing.
"Lord, teach us to pray."
